scope: Historical baseline for the 13 networking/security modules, plus initial Systems Administration entries. This is not release approval.
protected: Existing certificate verification and PDF records

globalFindings.finding: The existing assessment issues Network Fundamentals certificates after a quiz pass without a compulsory graded practical exercise.
globalFindings.action: Design versioned eligibility migration before changing issuance. Keep old records valid and label legacy attainment accurately; new-standard certificates must require server-verified practical success.

globalFindings.finding: No course has the complete required theory/practical/explanation grading and guided-activity eligibility pipeline.
globalFindings.action: Implement server-owned attempts and controlled scenario variation, outcome verification, retry history, rubric review, and a practical pass gate. Do not grade prose quality by length or award credit from browser success flags.

globalFindings.finding: Account activity accepts only network, mitm, and ddos. Course-specific persisted assessed outcomes do not exist for the other modules.
globalFindings.action: Introduce stable identifiers for all 13 and migrate reporting without changing identity keys.

globalFindings.finding: Only the advanced topology workshop supports bounded construction and rewiring. Course illustrations are not a reusable multi-device environment.
globalFindings.action: Introduce shared interface, link, packet, and device state with explicit compatibility rules. Keep specialized protocol models rather than forcing everything into one fake universal engine.

globalFindings.finding: Playback implementations differ, with inconsistent speed, backward inspection, timeline, and state commit behavior.
globalFindings.action: Extract a tested replay controller. Backward inspection must not retransmit, refresh leases, repeat MAC learning, or award completion.

globalFindings.finding: Most new laboratories reset on navigation and lack validated save/restore and before/after comparisons.
globalFindings.action: Add versioned bounded practice checkpoints with validation, explicit restore, and baseline comparisons. Keep practice files separate from assessed records.

globalFindings.finding: Guided procedures do not consistently contain all A-J experiment sections or embedded knowledge checks.
globalFindings.action: Author course-specific experiment briefs and knowledge checks, with human technical and instructional review; headings alone do not satisfy content depth.

criteria.content: Comprehensive tutorial, terminology, references, and knowledge checks
criteria.environment: Configurable devices, interfaces, compatible connections, and realistic state
criteria.animation: State-driven replay, speed, backward inspection, event timeline, and comparison
criteria.guided: Multiple A-J structured guided experiments with verification
criteria.independent: Varied mandatory exercise with protected solution, independent repair, and stored outcome
criteria.grading: Theory, practical, explanation, eligibility, and certificate gate
criteria.qa: Documented positive, failure, boundary, interruption, repeat, accessibility, and regression results
criteria.completion: All release acceptance checks evidenced and signed off

courses.title: Network Fundamentals
courses.current: Device roles, local/remote path and link toggle; a separate advanced workshop supports up to eight switches and 24 hosts, endpoint addressing/VLANs, routing, messages, import/export, and local checks.
courses.limits: Course illustration is a scripted path, not the workshop engine. No OS, interface speed/duplex, cable compatibility, assessed independent repair, or full course rubric.
courses.next: Integrate the bounded workshop as the foundational configurable environment; add interface inspection and connection validation, then server-verified independent repair.

courses.title: Network Communication
courses.current: OSI/TCP-IP explanations and sender/switch/router/receiver trace with example IP, TCP ports and TTL.
courses.limits: Predetermined packet and topology; no editable headers or faults, persistent evidence, independent verification, or course assessment.
courses.next: Add a structured packet inspector, controlled source/destination/TTL changes, and an independent header/fault investigation.

courses.title: IP Addressing
courses.current: IPv4/IPv6, historical classes, address types, binary conversion, bit/mask visualization, subnet ranges, classful/CIDR and VLSM exercises.
courses.limits: Calculation labs do not configure linked devices. Worked solutions are available before submission. No protected varied practical or separate theory assessment.
courses.next: Add a varied address-plan challenge checked against endpoint reachability, including negative tests for duplicates, masks, boundaries and IPv6 scope limitations.

courses.title: VLANs
courses.current: Access/trunk, purpose-based VLANs, isolation, trunk allowance and inter-VLAN routing toggles; workshop provides related host configuration.
courses.limits: Guided demo assumes correct IP settings and a gateway on Switch B. No reusable trunk/interface model or independently scored repair.
courses.next: Unify endpoint, access and trunk configuration with a reusable topology; verify permitted and forbidden paths together.

courses.title: Routing
courses.current: Route families, longest-prefix choice, TTL expiry, static failure, compressed withdrawal, and worked distance/link/path-vector examples.
courses.limits: Fixed route table and worked exchange narratives. No route editor, real routing protocol state machines, loop/return-path model, saved configuration, or graded challenge.
courses.next: Add editable connected/static/default routes and validated next-hop reachability; keep protocol walkthroughs explicitly bounded.

courses.title: Switching and MAC Address Learning
courses.current: Four access ports, source learning, known/unknown unicast, broadcast, VLAN settings, links, aging, predictions and log.
courses.limits: No trunks, STP, device construction or vendor CLI. Guided repair is not a randomized assessed exercise; settings are not saved across visits.
courses.next: Preserve this tested forwarding model while adding common interface objects, checkpoint import/export, and an independently verified fault scenario.

courses.title: DHCP Operations
courses.current: Two-address pool, allocation, renewal, T1/T2 conditions, expiry, relay/server faults and gateway diagnosis.
courses.limits: One fixed scope, no scope editor or real broadcast packets; no persistent independent task. State commits only at completed trace.
courses.next: Add configurable pool exclusions/reservations, explicit interface context, varied exhaustion/relay/option repair, and saved evidence.

courses.title: DNS Operations
courses.current: A/AAAA, one CNAME, query-key caching, positive/negative TTL, NXDOMAIN, resolver timeout and authority failure.
courses.limits: Three fixed names; simplified negative TTL/referrals; no zone editor, DNSSEC validation or independent assessed repair.
courses.next: Add bounded editable records and resolver configuration with type-aware verification, cache timeline and independent wrong-answer investigation.

courses.title: Network Firewalls and ACLs
courses.current: Two ordered stateless profiles, source prefix/protocol/port matching, reversal, rule shadowing and decision evidence.
courses.limits: No arbitrary rule editing, egress/destination matching, stateful session model, device interfaces or independent scored exercise.
courses.next: Add a validated rule editor, permitted AND prohibited regression probes, and policy repair that cannot pass by allowing everything.

courses.title: NAT/PAT
courses.current: TCP endpoint-bound PAT, two public ports, tuple reuse, return match, expiry and exhaustion.
courses.limits: No TCP state machine, checksum, static NAT/port forward, route integration, arbitrary pool, or independent assessed repair.
courses.next: Preserve mapping semantics and add configurable bounded pools, interface context and positive/negative return-flow verification.

courses.title: Network Monitoring and Troubleshooting
courses.current: Deterministic synthetic probes, baseline, loss/RTT/adjacent variation, DNS-vs-network failures and comparison.
courses.limits: Preset samples are not generated from a shared network/queue. No captures/device counters or independently varied graded investigation.
courses.next: Connect measurements to bounded network conditions and store reproducible baseline/fault/repair evidence, without claiming root cause from one metric.

courses.title: Man-in-the-Middle (MiTM)
courses.current: Synthetic ARP redirection, plaintext/TLS visibility rules, forwarding disruption, pinned mapping, guided lessons, local diagnosis/recovery checks, saved notes/baselines, packet replay.
courses.limits: No cryptography or OS interception. Fixed inspectable challenge cases and local completion markers are not protected independently assessed attempts.
courses.next: Preserve safe isolation and existing study keys; add server-owned varied scenarios, recorded evidence, and a reviewed explanation rubric.

courses.title: DoS/DDoS
courses.current: Fluid service/queue model, single/distributed sources, upstream limits, rate limiting, loss accounting, synthetic flow animation, baselines and local fault/recovery checks.
courses.limits: Aggregate fractional rates, not packet traces or real attacks. Fixed local cases, no protected graded attempt or independent course credential.
courses.next: Preserve demand and conservation invariants; add varied server-owned overload/limiter scenarios and verify both recovery and unchanged legitimate workload.

courses.title: Linux Server Administration
courses.current: Five Ubuntu Server 24.04 modules with 19 terminal walkthroughs, seven configurable browser labs, saved practice evidence, and an independent handover with two incidents and a 100-point rubric.
courses.limits: Command outputs are illustrative. There is no provisioned Ubuntu guest or verification against live guest state. The optional server-graded certificate assessment currently evaluates simulated service recovery.
courses.next: Run the commands on a pinned disposable Ubuntu image, validate actual outputs, and complete independent administrator, beginner, and assistive-technology reviews. See review/linux-server-administration.md.

courses.title: Automation and Scripting
courses.current: Bash and Python worked examples and guided log audit, safe repeatability, and scheduled job fault repair.
courses.limits: Fixture-driven job models. The graded exercise checks failure handling and concurrent scheduled runs.
courses.next: Review the Bash and Python examples and observe learners diagnosing repeated and overlapping jobs.

courses.title: Backup, Restore & Recovery
courses.current: Guided recovery budget, damaged incremental chain, and cross-course staging and cutover capstone.
courses.limits: Synthetic backup objects and service probes. The graded repair verifies a simulated incremental restore.
courses.next: Review the exercises with a recovery operator and observe learners explaining their verification and cutover decisions.

implementationPlan.deliverable: Shared device/interface/link/packet contracts and course-specific configurable environments
implementationPlan.acceptance: Compatibility, duplicate addressing, disabled links, VLANs, routes, faults and repair tested across integrated paths.

implementationPlan.deliverable: Course-by-course independent practical assessment and versioned credential eligibility
implementationPlan.acceptance: Server controls scenario/attempt, verifies outcomes and required negative probes, records retries, and requires practical pass; explanation rubric has reviewed criteria.

implementationPlan.deliverable: Full A-J experiments, embedded knowledge checks, references and professional technical review for each course
implementationPlan.acceptance: Each actual procedure identifies equipment/configuration, observations, explanation and verification; content depth independently reviewed.

implementationPlan.deliverable: All-course functional/accessibility validation, beginner observation and staging/identity/provider deployment review
implementationPlan.acceptance: Recorded results and named human sign-off; no unresolved release-blocking defects.
